interactions.summary: A student explains that salvation starts when people choose to look toward God, Jiang turns that answer into a full cosmology of universal welcome plus total free choice, and the room then tests why God would want such freedom through voluntary-love and energy-accumulation models.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led classroom exchange with multiple student replies

speaker_notes.note: These lines are speculative student improvisations and may partly overlap in the diarization, but the general claim is that divine will might somehow operate through human freedom.

claims.claim: A student argues that when people decide they want salvation and want not to sin, they respond by looking toward God rather than waiting for God to watch over them.
Jiang states that God is always welcoming and always trying to draw the soul, but whether one moves toward or away from that light is entirely a matter of free choice.
Jiang calls free choice the fundamental law of the universe and insists that everything a person does is chosen, even when it does not feel like a choice.
Jiang says Beatrice's task is to elaborate this premise that everything one does is a matter of chosen desire and will.
A student answers that God gives free will so love and obedience can be willing rather than forced, which would make heaven and command-following meaningful.
Another student imagines God as energy that agents with free will gravitate toward, causing that source to grow larger.
A later speculative reply suggests that God may somehow use human beings as the site where freedom gets expressed.

signature_moments.moment: God is redefined as constant welcome rather than constant surveillance.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's cleanest statement of grace as invitation rather than policing.

signature_moments.moment: Free choice is elevated from one human faculty to the basic law of the universe.
signature_moments.source_phrase: This is the fundamental law of the universe. It's all, everything is free choice
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the lecture its governing metaphysical rule and explains why heaven and hell must be self-authored.

signature_moments.moment: One student translates theology into a physics picture where God is energy and souls gravitate toward a growing source.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The metaphor shows the class testing Jiang's model with a more modern causal language.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's name for the ultimate law of the universe: every movement toward or away from God comes from chosen desire and will.
The destination one approaches by welcoming God, contrasted with turning away through misuse of freedom.
Jiang's paired terms for the inner faculty through which free choice becomes action and orientation toward God.

chronology_notes.note: This packet formalizes the same June 15 argument into a general law of free choice without introducing a dated change relative to other Jiang sources.

uncertainty_notes.note: The speculation about God lacking or using free will is not stable doctrine in this packet and reads as exploratory student talk rather than settled interpretation.
